tools.name: agent.compact
tools.description: Record a compaction checkpoint for this agent: the agent is about to have its context summarized, so it writes a durable marker (id, agentId, ts, summary, nextHint) that agent.resume later follows to reconstruct the identity + state. This is the explicit continuation handshake — a crash/compaction for THIS agent is recorded so a later prompt in the same thread can resume cleanly instead of starting anonymous.

nextHint.description: Optional hint for the next step (e.g. the next file to touch). Returned on resume verbatim.

summary.description: Short summary of what this agent did / where it left off (the checkpoint's durable record). Saved as-is and returned on resume.

tools.name: agent.heartbeat
tools.description: Update this agent's roster entry: lastSeen, status (idle|working|blocked|done), and the current task summary. Other agents see this via agent.status/agent.list. Cheap — call it between steps so the roster stays live.

tools.name: agent.list
tools.description: List the workspace agent roster chronologically: every agent identity (id, name, sid, createdAt, lastSeen, status, task, toolCount) that has touched this workspace. Sorted newest-first.

tools.name: agent.lock
tools.description: Take an advisory lock on a path (e.g. a file you are about to edit). {holdMs} auto-releases the lock after that long even if this agent crashes (default 10 min). Locking is advisory — it makes the intent visible and recordable so agents choose not to collide. Check agent.locks/agent.status before editing, and agent.unlock when done.

holdMs.description: Auto-release after this many ms even if this agent crashes (default 10 min).

path.description: Path (relative to base dir or absolute) this agent will be editing.

tools.name: agent.locks
tools.description: List active advisory locks: path, agentId, heldAt, expiresAt, expired state. Call this before writing to a path to see whether another agent is mid-edit there.

tools.name: agent.messages
tools.description: Read inter-agent messages. {since} filters by agentId context (from/to), {lastN} caps the tail. Returns messages newest-first with from/to/kind.

to.description: Return messages to (direct) or from this agentId. Omit = all.

tools.name: agent.peers
tools.description: List agents across OTHER workspaces from the GLOBAL index (~/.nc-tools/agents.jsonl, override with NCTOOLS_AGENT_HOME). Agents register here too, so you can discover who else is working on a different project and coordinate with them. Filter by {workspace} to narrow. Cross-process + cross-machine-user.

workspace.description: Narrow to agents last seen in this workspace path (substring match).

tools.name: agent.post
tools.description: Post a message to the inter-agent noticeboard. {to} may be an agentId for a direct message or omitted for a broadcast. {kind} is note|question|request|handoff|bug|hold|resume — other agents can filter by it. Messages persist in .nc-tools/agent-messages.jsonl.

kind.description: note | question | request | handoff | bug | hold | resume

to.description: Recipient agentId; omit for a broadcast.

tools.name: agent.register
tools.description: Register (or resume) this agent's identity in the workspace roster AND the global (cross-workspace) index. With {agentId} restores a known identity (the crash/compaction continuation path — a client that remembers who it was keeps its identity and history). Without it, resumes this session's agent or mints `agent-<n>` (chronological). Returns {agentId, name, role, createdAt, resumed}. Call agent.status to see who else is working here; agent.peers to see agents on OTHER workspaces.

agentId.description: A known agent id to restore (crash/compaction continuation). When present and in the roster, the identity is resumed with a new lastSeen.

name.description: Human label for the roster (default: derived from agentId or a counter).

tools.name: agent.resume
tools.description: Follow this agent's most recent compaction checkpoint: confirms identity continuity after a crash/compaction, re-registers the same agentId, and returns its last summary + nextHint so the resumed agent can pick up where it left off. Call agent.resume at the start of a prompt when you believe you are continuing a prior thread.

agentId.description: Which agent to resume. Defaults to this session's agent (by sid) if omitted. When omitted and no prior checkpoint exists, no-op.

tools.name: agent.status
tools.description: Full coordination snapshot: who is here, what each is working on, active locks, whether this agent is locked out of any path, and recent inter-agent messages. The 'look around before you start' tool.

tools.name: agent.unlock
tools.description: Release a lock this agent holds on a path. If the lock has expired (holdMs passed) this is a no-op; if another agent holds it, it is NOT released (you cannot steal a live lock).

tools.name: batch.execute
tools.description: Run up to 25 kernel tool calls in ONE round-trip: [{tool, args, dependsOn?}]. Each sub-call is individually executed and journaled; failures do not abort the batch. Calls with no dependsOn execute in parallel; calls with dependsOn=[indices] wait for those to finish first. Use for independent multi-step work.

dependsOn.description: Indices of calls this one depends on (0-based). The call waits until all dependencies finish before executing. Empty/absent = independent.

tools.name: code.symbols
tools.description: Extract code symbols (fns, structs, enums, traits, impls, mods, classes, interfaces, defs) with line numbers AND line spans + doc comments - a fast lexical scan with brace/indent extension, not a full parser. Each symbol returns {name, kind, line, endLine, doc, span-bytes} so you can read exactly the matched range. Languages: Rust, JS/TS/TSX/JSX, Python.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

kinds.description: Only return these kinds, e.g. fn, struct

path.description: Path - relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

withBody.description: Include the full text of each symbol (default true; set false for a lean name/kind/line-only listing).

tools.name: env.get
tools.description: Read an environment variable (session override wins over host).

tools.name: env.list
tools.description: List session environment overrides.

tools.name: env.set
tools.description: Set a session environment variable; all subsequent proc.* calls inherit it.

guardLocks.description: When true, refuse the write if ANOTHER agent holds a live advisory lock on this path (hard-write-guard). Default false = advisory: the write proceeds but the result carries a lockConflict note.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

guardLocks.description: When true, refuse the delete if ANOTHER agent holds a live advisory lock on this path (hard-write-guard). Default false = advisory.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.description: List directory entries.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.description: Create a directory.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

tools.name: fs.read
tools.description: Read a text file with line numbers. Supports offset/limit paging. Returns a digest (hash+mtime) — use it to avoid re-reading unchanged files.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace). Lets an agent bound to one workspace read files in another without re-rooting the server.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: fs.readMany
tools.description: Read up to 50 files in ONE call. Each item returns ok/content or a structured error. Prefer this over N separate fs.read calls.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

tools.name: fs.readRange
tools.description: Read a BYTE RANGE of a file without loading it whole - for huge files and logs. Returns the decoded window, byte offsets (chain via nextByteOffset), the 1-based line number where the window starts, and eof. Use fs.read for line-based paging of normal files.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

byteOffset.description: Byte offset to start from (0 = file start)

path.description: Path - relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: fs.stat
tools.description: Stat a path (exists, type, size).

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: fs.tree
tools.description: Render a bounded directory tree in one call: depth-capped, entry-capped, skips .git/node_modules/target/dist/.nc-tools. Returns structured entries (path/type/size/depth) plus an ASCII rendering. Directories sort first.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Path - relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: fs.write
tools.description: Write a file (creates parent dirs). Returns created/overwrote.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

guardLocks.description: When true, refuse the write if ANOTHER agent holds a live advisory lock on this path (hard-write-guard). Default false = advisory: the write proceeds but the result carries a lockConflict note.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: fs.writeMany
tools.description: Write up to 50 files in ONE call: [{path, content}]. Per-item ok/error results.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

baseDir.description: Base directory override (default: kernel base dir). Pass when working on a different workspace than the server was started on.

tools.name: net.cite
tools.description: Record a durable, machine-checkable citation: net.cite {url} stores id + title + content hash + a ready-to-paste citation line (content itself lives in the fetch cache, so the quote survives link rot); net.cite {id} re-checks a stored source (unchanged / changed / dead); net.cite {} lists the ledger. Pair with net.verify to confirm a claim is actually grounded before citing.

id.description: Citation id to re-check (unchanged / changed / dead); omit to list the ledger

url.description: URL to cite (records the source); omit to list the ledger

tools.name: net.fetch
tools.description: Read a web page as CLEAN MARKDOWN for an agent: main-content extraction discards nav/ads/boilerplate, returns title, links, token estimate, and extraction confidence. SSRF-guarded by default (private/loopback targets refused; allowPrivate to reach internal hosts), ETag-revalidated cache (set refresh to force), Accept: text/markdown negotiation, and automatic headless re-render through the system browser when a JS-heavy page extracts as empty. Prefer over net.http whenever you want page CONTENT, not raw protocol bytes.

allowPrivate.description: Allow private/loopback targets (for local dev servers); default blocks them

maxTokens.description: Estimate token cap for the markdown (truncates output)

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and revalidate with the server

render.description: Re-render JS-heavy pages through the system browser's headless mode when extraction looks empty (default true; no-op when no browser is installed)

tools.name: net.http
tools.description: Perform a raw HTTP request. Returns status, headers, body (capped), duration, redirect chain. blockPrivate=true refuses private/loopback targets. Replaces curl/wget; use net.fetch when you want readable page content.

blockPrivate.description: Refuse private/loopback/link-local targets (SSRF guard); default false to keep raw-curl semantics

tools.name: net.probePort
tools.description: Check whether a TCP port is open. Replaces nc/netstat probing.

tools.name: net.robots
tools.description: Check what a site allows an agent to fetch: robots.txt isAllowed for a URL (RFC 9309 longest-match), crawl-delay, sitemap URLs, and llms.txt discovery (the site's own curated agent index). Fetch this before crawling or fetching many pages from one host.

allowPrivate.description: Allow private/loopback targets (for local dev servers)

tools.name: net.search
tools.description: Search the WEB keylessly: fans the query across free engines (DuckDuckGo Lite, Mojeek, Wikipedia, Hacker News), fuses results with reciprocal-rank fusion, then RERANKS them locally with a MiniLM transformer (same offline neural stack as search.semantic) so the best answer ranks first without any API key. Returns title, url, snippet, engines, score. Use for anything outside the workspace; pair with net.fetch to read the top hits.

engines.description: Comma-separated engine names, "all" for every healthy source, "auto" (default) for intent-routed selection

fetchTop.description: Auto-read the top N results (0-3) and attach their markdown (progressive disclosure; costs one fetch each)

intent.description: Force an intent: general | news | howto | academic | package (default auto-classified locally)

rerank.description: Local neural rerank after fusion, with authority boost (default true; falls back to fusion order if the model is unavailable)

tools.name: net.verify
tools.description: Check whether a CLAIM is actually grounded in a web page (anti-hallucination before citing): fetches (or reads the cached copy of a cited source), chunks the content, embeds claim and chunks with the local MiniLM, and returns grounded / partial / not-grounded with the best-matching span. Needs the local embedding model; net.cite {id} is the model-free health check.

tools.name: patch.apply
tools.description: Apply exact-match search/replace edits to a file. Each edit: {oldText, newText, expectedCount?}. Fails with structured hints (occurrence counts, nearest candidate lines, and a char-level diff of WHICH part differs) if not found or ambiguous. When fuzzy=true, an edit whose oldText is within fuzzyThreshold edits of a candidate is applied with a corrections report — survives whitespace/formatting drift.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

fuzzy.description: When true, an oldText that differs from a candidate by <= fuzzyThreshold single-character edits is applied with a corrections report (survives whitespace/formatting drift). Exact match is still preferred.

guardLocks.description: When true, refuse the patch if ANOTHER agent holds a live advisory lock on this path (hard-write-guard). Default false = advisory.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: patch.applyMany
tools.description: Apply patch edits to up to 20 files in ONE call: [{path, edits:[{oldText,newText,expectedCount?}]}]. Per-file ok/error results.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

fuzzy.description: When true, an oldText that differs from a candidate by <= fuzzyThreshold single-character edits is applied with a corrections report (survives whitespace/formatting drift). Exact match is still preferred.

tools.name: pkg.add
tools.description: Install packages (npm or pip). Structured result; ERR_NETWORK hint if registry unreachable.

tools.name: pkg.list

tools.name: pkg.runScript

tools.name: pkg.scripts
tools.description: List npm scripts defined in package.json.

tools.name: proc.kill

tools.name: proc.list

tools.name: proc.readOutput

tools.name: proc.runScript
tools.description: Run an interpreted script (js/python/shell/powershell/batch) with a hard timeout. Provide a file path OR inline source. Captures stdout/stderr + exit code.

baseDir.description: Base directory override (default: kernel base dir)

language.description: Language: js|python|shell|powershell|batch (inferred from path extension if omitted)

path.description: Script file - relative to the base dir, or absolute

source.description: Inline source (used when no path is given)

tools.name: proc.spawn
tools.description: Run a program with typed argv (no shell). Captures stdout/stderr, exit code, hard timeout.

baseDir.description: Base directory override (default: kernel base dir). Pass when working on a different workspace than the server was started on.

cwd.description: Working dir (absolute allowed; default base dir)

tools.name: proc.start
tools.description: Start a LONG-RUNNING background process (server, watcher). Returns a handleId. NOT for one-shot commands — use proc.spawn for those.

baseDir.description: Base directory override (default: kernel base dir)

cwd.description: Working dir (absolute allowed; default base dir)

tools.name: proc.status
tools.description: Status of a background process handle: running, exitCode, outputBytes, uptime.

tools.name: proc.stop
tools.description: Stop a background process by handle.

tools.name: proc.watch
tools.description: Watch a file/dir and re-run a long-lived command whenever the tree changes (auto-rebuild / dev server). Returns a handleId managed by proc.status/readOutput/stop.

baseDir.description: Base directory override (default: kernel base dir)

cmd.description: Command to keep running (a server / rebuild loop)

path.description: File or directory to watch (recursive)

tools.name: search.files
tools.description: Find files by glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.test.mjs"). Directory scans are bounded like search.grep; scanTruncated:true means the scan budget stopped early.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: search.grep
tools.description: Regex search across files. Returns file/line/text matches. Directory scans are bounded: they skip .git/node_modules/.nc-tools/target/dist/build, skip files over 10MB, and stop after 20k files or 10s (limits.grepMaxScan*) — scanTruncated:true in the result means the budget stopped the scan, so matches may be partial. Directly-targeted file paths are always scanned in full. Supports contextBefore/contextAfter (adjacent lines with line numbers), fileType (extension filter, e.g. "rs"), and fixedString (fast literal substring search — no regex compilation).

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

contextAfter.description: Lines of context after a match (0 = none).

contextBefore.description: Lines of context before a match (0 = none).

fileType.description: Filter by extension (e.g. "rs", "ts", "py" — no dot). Overrides glob.

fixedString.description: Literal substring search (no regex compilation — much faster). The pattern is matched as a plain string, not a regex.

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: search.replace
tools.description: Regex search/replace across files. dryRun=true (default) reports per-file match counts without writing; dryRun=false rewrites files (run sys.snapshot first for rollback). Supports $0-$9 capture backrefs ($$ = literal $). Skips binaries and .git/node_modules/target/dist/build/.nc-tools.

baseDir.description: Base dir for the root path (default: the session workspace).

dryRun.description: true (default) = report only; false = write the changes

path.description: Root of the search (default: base dir)

tools.name: search.semantic
tools.description: Locate code by MEANING, not exact text: ask where something is handled (e.g. 'where is journal write integrity validated?') and get the EXACT function/struct/line-range ranked by semantic relevance. Each file is chunked at symbol boundaries and each chunk is embedded separately, so the result names the symbol (validate_token, AuthHandler, etc.) and its line range, not just the file. Prefer this over search.grep when you do not know the exact identifier or wording. Runs a local MiniLM transformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) fully offline — no API calls; ranking is deterministic per content digest. Drill into top hits with fs.read {offset} to read the matched lines.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Path — relative to the base dir, or absolute (any location allowed)

tools.name: sys.doctor
tools.description: Self-diagnostics: registered tools, config limits, session env, journal stats. deep=true also probes runtime (workspace writable, cargo on PATH).

deep.description: Include runtime probes (writable root, cargo available)

tools.name: sys.journal
tools.description: Read the session journal (your own tool-call trail).

tools.name: sys.listSnapshots
tools.description: List available snapshots.

tools.name: sys.rollback
tools.description: Restore the workspace to a snapshot: restores manifest files, removes files created after the snapshot. Pass paths to restore only those files and leave the rest untouched (partial rollback).

paths.description: Restore only these paths from the snapshot; other files are left as-is. This makes a bad edit undoable WITHOUT losing unrelated work.

tools.name: sys.snapshot
tools.description: Capture a workspace snapshot (files + dirs, excludes .git/node_modules/.nc-tools). Returns an id usable with sys.rollback. Use before risky edits so you can undo.

tools.name: sys.snapshotDiff
tools.description: Diff two snapshots: what files were added, removed, or modified between them, plus byte totals. Answers 'what changed since I snapshotted before the deploy?' — the review gate before a rollback.

tools.name: sys.workspace
tools.description: Workspace info: root path, platform.

tools.name: test.run
tools.description: Run a test suite and get STRUCTURED results: passed/failed counts, failing test names + messages. Frameworks: node (node:test), pytest.

path.description: Test file/dir path (absolute allowed); default = standard patterns in base dir

tools.name: text.diff
tools.description: Unified diff between two files (or a file and a string). Returns a git-style @@ hunk diff plus parseable counts. Paths are relative to the base dir or absolute.

baseDir.description: Base dir for relative paths (default: the session workspace).

path.description: Left file - relative to the base dir, or absolute

path2.description: Right file - relative to the base dir, or absolute

wordLevel.description: Word-level diff: when a line pair differs, run a Myers diff on WORD tokens instead of showing the whole line as changed. Returns structured segments (same/added/removed) for each changed line pair.
